requirements.title: Interoperable ordinary arguments and scalar results correspond across C and Fortran
requirements.source: 18.3.7 p2 items (2)(a), (4), and the interoperable-entity alternative of (5); p3. Eligibility also depends on 18.3.6.
requirements.definition: For an eligible BIND(C) interface matching a C prototype, VALUE scalars, non-VALUE interoperable array arguments, and an interoperable scalar result correspond to the appropriate C values, pointers, and result in matching argument positions.
requirements.oracle: Compile a Fortran interface/wrapper module, a C function, and a Fortran caller separately. The C function receives a count by value and an integer array by pointer, mutates the array, and returns a checksum. Check independently specified values and stdout after linking the declared objects.

accounting.rationale: BIND is an eligibility condition for this calibrated interface.
Only the ordinary-argument subset is mapped; the remaining alternatives are explicit subdivisions.
Matching prototype arity is a fixture eligibility condition.
C descriptors, assumed type/rank, and other pointer alternatives require additional fixtures.
Deferred character-length eligibility is not covered.
The variable-argument restriction needs its own admission/diagnostic analysis.
Descriptor characteristics when C invokes Fortran are not covered.
Contiguity/temporary behavior remains to be catalogued.
Further interoperable-reference semantics remain to be catalogued.
